summary: Ryojin Soga was a Buddhist studies scholar and philosopher. He studied at Otani University, Shinshu University, and under Manshi Kiyozawa. He served as professor and president at Otani University, and also held a professorship at Toyo University.

Ryojun Mitomo specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. His academic career includes professorships at Rissho University Junior College (attested 1996) and Rissho University's Faculty of Social Welfare (attested 2001).
Ryojun Okubo worked in the field of Buddhist studies. He studied under Morito Ninomiya and served as department head at Taisho University (attested 1978–1984).

Ryokei Kaginushi was a scholar in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He taught Nobuyoshi Yamabe and served as a professor at Otani University, attested in 1978 in the Faculty of Letters and from 1987 to 1993.

Ryoken Nawa is a Buddhist studies scholar. His academic positions include serving as a commissioned researcher at Kyoto Koka Women's University (attested 2015) and holding a post at Osaka University (attested 2020).
Ryoko Mochizuki is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology. After studying at the University of Tokyo until 1963, Mochizuki served as a lecturer at Rissho University, attested in 1972 and 1983.

Ryomin Akizuki was a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1947–1950). He taught Makio Takemura and held a position at Saitama Medical University from around 1973 to 1987.

Ryosaburo Sakaki worked in Buddhist studies, Indology, and linguistics. He studied at the Third Higher School and the University of Tokyo, later serving as professor at the Third Higher School (1899) and Kyoto University (1908).

Ryosei Fukuda was a Buddhist studies scholar who earned his degrees at Toyo University. He became a professor at Taisho University in 1973, later professor emeritus, and served as director of the Kawasaki Daishi Institute of Buddhist Studies.

Ryoshin Nakao is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Komazawa University (1971–1975). He served as a professor at Hanazono University (~1990–2018) and held researcher positions at Soto Zen institutes.

Ryosho Hayashi was a Buddhist studies and history/archaeology scholar who studied at Taisho University and Tokyo Metropolitan University. At Taisho University, he became professor in 1975, dean of literature in 1981, and president from 1990 to 1994.

Ryosho Nakamura specialized in Indology and philosophy. He studied at the Seventh Higher School, Tohoku University under Ensho Kanakura, and Rissho University. He served as a professor at The International University of Kagoshima from around 1962 to 1998.

Ryosho Tanaka was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Komazawa University. He held multiple posts at Komazawa University, including professor (from 1964), dean, museum director, and president (2009), as well as a professorship at Ryukoku University.

Ryoshu Kouda is an Indology and Buddhist studies researcher who studied under Seitatsu Matsunami. He served as a researcher at Taisho University (attested 1998) and at the Hasegawa Buddhist Cultural Institute (attested 2006).

Ryoshu Michihata was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology who studied at Otani University. He held an academic post at Otani University from ~1935 to 1974 and served as a professor at Kyoto Koka Women's University (~1974–1984).
Ryoshu Misaki was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Waseda University. He subsequently served on the faculty at Waseda University from around 1958 to 1991, later becoming professor emeritus.

Ryoshun Okubo is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Waseda University (~1973–1983). He became Professor of Sino-Japanese Buddhism at Waseda University (~1997) and served as director of Taimon Kenkyūkai (attested 2007).
Ryosuke Furui is a scholar of Indology and history/archaeology. He completed a PhD at Jawaharlal Nehru University in 2007 and held a post at the University of Tokyo, attested in 2011.

Ryota Nakamura is a Buddhist studies researcher. Attested in 2015, he pursued doctoral studies and served as a graduate student researcher at Toyo University, while also holding a researcher post at the Shinran Buddhist Center.

Ryotai Hatani was a Buddhist studies scholar who taught Gadjin M. Nagao and Ryogon Fukuhara. He served on the faculty at Ryukoku University (~1920–1954), becoming professor emeritus, and held a post at Kyoto University from 1929 to 1943.
